actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.name: seed

facts.text: DroneHoverSimpleEnv-v0 is the hover task with PWM control at 100 Hz, simple physics, 100 Hz observations, 10% domain randomization, no aerodynamic effects and instant motor force
The CrazyFlie agent has four control channels (act_dim=4)
The action space bounds each of the four control channels to [-1, 1]
The observation history keeps two (observation, action) pairs
The observation space is a Box bounded by +-1000 whose width is the history length times the observation plus action width
With observation noise enabled, the observation concatenates position, quaternion, linear velocity and angular rate
The hover target is the position [0, 0, 1.0]
The hover episode terminates when roll or pitch passes 60 degrees, altitude falls below 0.2 m or an angular rate passes 300 degrees per second
The reward is minus the Euclidean distance to the target minus the action, angle, spin, velocity and terminal penalties
A reset draws a position offset of +-0.25 m, roll and pitch of +-pi/6 rad, yaw of +-2pi rad, linear velocity of +-0.1 m/s and angular rate of +-200 deg/s (yaw +-20 deg/s)
reset accepts a seed keyword but the body does not read it
The initial state is drawn with numpy's global random generator through np.random.uniform and np.random.normal
Observation noise is enabled by default (observation_noise=1)
The simple hover environment uses SimplePhysics with the cf21x_sys_eq drone model and sim_freq=100 Hz

determinism.notes: this package's fake draws the reset state from random.Random(seed) and its dynamics are deterministic, so one seed and action sequence repeat a trajectory; upstream reset() accepts but ignores seed (base.py:382-429) and draws from numpy's global generator, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: the fake integrates the simplified rigid-body equations of SimplePhysics with an ideal PWM-to-thrust map: no contacts, drag, ground effect or motor dynamics, and the 10% domain randomization of the upstream environment is not applied
observation noise (observation_noise=1 upstream, hover.py:12) is not modelled; the fake returns the 13-value noiseless observation that the upstream 100 Hz branch would produce

upstream reset() accepts but ignores seed and draws the initial state from numpy's global generator (base.py:382-429, hover.py:203-228); the fake uses random.Random(seed), so a seed does not repeat an upstream trajectory
the fake was not compared with the upstream PyBullet environment and no physical device is modelled; nothing was validated
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms (10 ms) only
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
